bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay

When you’re offered an hourly rate or a salary, it helps to see the full picture: what you’ll earn in a year, what you’ll take home after tax, and how super and salary sacrifice Australia fit in. This guide explains the standard conversion and the key figures you need to know.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours a week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). So if you earn $30 an hour, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. That’s before tax, Medicare, and any salary sacrifice arrangements.

If you’re paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the example above, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get an extra 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Many awards set higher minimum rates for specific industries or roles. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. The figures here are averages or minimums, not a job median.

### Casual Loading: How It Works

Casual loading (25%) is paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. On [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and check the box to add 25% loading. Never type a rate that already includes loading – the calculator does that for you. For example, a base rate of $26.44 becomes $33.05 with loading.

### Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates: no tax on the first $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted – these are estimates only.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% on ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). Super is paid on top of your salary, not taken from it. So if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 in super. The estimate shows super separately.

### Salary Sacrifice Australia

Salary sacrifice Australia allows you to reduce your taxable income by swapping salary for benefits like a car, laptop, or extra super contributions. It can lower your tax, but it’s not included in the basic hourly-to-annual calculation. If you salary sacrifice, your take-home pay will differ from the estimate. Talk to your employer or a tax professional about how it applies to you.

### Average Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. All employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, experience, and location.

### Using the Timesheet

[The timesheet](/) is the main tool. Enter your base hourly rate, choose whether to add casual loading, and see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly estimates. The results include estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember the disclaimer: no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice are included. Super is estimated at 12% on ordinary earnings only, stopping at the maximum contribution base.

### Final Notes

Always check with the Fair Work Ombudsman for your correct award classification and with the Australian Taxation Office for your personal tax situation. The figures here are based on published data and are a guide, not a guarantee. Use the calculator to get a quick estimate, then confirm with your employer or adviser.
